front_line: The restaurant's operating system — and a toll on every check
thesis: Toast has the traction of a clear winner; my hesitation is price and durability, not the business. I want a better entry plus proof the unit economics hold — GPV per location staying healthy, ARR per location no longer diluting as enterprise and international scale, and a durable payments take-rate against Square and Clover. Confirm those and it graduates off the bench; if GPV per location rolls over or the take-rate compresses, it stays here.
moat: Genuine switching-cost moat on the customer; fragile and contestable on the take rate.
risks: Take rate is the most contestable variable and Square (equally scaled) could spark a price war.

categories.label: Moat
categories.note: Stickiness and switching costs, not a structural monopoly

categories.label: Risk
categories.note: Slower GPV per location, and ARPU drag. Competitors at heels

drafts.x_post: $TOST is the operating system restaurants run on — profitable now, four accelerating earnings beats, and a deepening switching-cost moat. Dead Simple Score 83. Watching for a better entry and proof the take rate holds. Aug 3 decides it.
video_talking_points: Toast is the technology a restaurant runs on — payments, ordering, kitchen displays, payroll, online orders, all in one system.
Why now: it's profitable, earnings have beaten estimates four quarters running with accelerating beats, and a former bear just flipped.
The bull point: every module a restaurant adds makes leaving harder, so the moat deepens as customers buy more.
The main risk: most revenue is thin-margin payment processing, and the per-check take rate is contestable if Square starts a price war.
The verdict: watch and buy a starter — the asymmetry is real and the catalyst is nine weeks out.
August 3 confirms or kills it: revenue up 20%+ with EPS, size up; single-digit revenue or dilution over 5%, walk.
